summary: This version of RobotPet guards its battery level with a property. Any attempt to set the battery below 0 or above 100 is quietly clamped into that range, so the value stored on the object is always valid.

lines.text: Even inside __init__, this assignment goes through the property setter below, so a pet created with a battery of 500 still starts at 100.
The @property decorator turns the method underneath into an attribute you read as pet.battery, with no parentheses.
The real value lives in _battery; the leading underscore signals that it is internal and should be reached through the property instead.
This registers the next method as the code that runs whenever anything assigns to pet.battery.
The first guard catches drained batteries.
Rather than raising an error, the setter clamps the value to the lowest legal level.
Only a value already inside the 0-to-100 range is stored unchanged.
Charging can stay this simple precisely because the setter enforces the limits; the method itself never has to check anything.
This reads the property, adds the amount, and assigns back through the setter, so a huge charge tops out at 100.

lines.code: return f"{self.name} performs a generic trick!"
lines.text: The base talent is deliberately generic, ready for subclasses to override in later exercises.
